title: Meaning of correct water in THALASSA
principle: Choose best validated mechanism per phenomenon, not newest build, approximate picture, or generic default water shader.
authority: The user's original intent plus historical champions; explicit measured evidence decides implementation details.
is_not_claiming: This is a semantic specification, not evidence that the final system is already physically or visually solved.

phenomena.meaning: Water is liquid mass in a continuous material, not a collection of white points or an animation texture.
phenomena.mechanism: Conserved liquid volume, momentum transport, pressure, gravity and interface stress; 2.5D and particles represent the same material at different resolutions.
phenomena.visual_signature: Motion redistributes a coherent volume; connected material remains connected until physically separated.
phenomena.failure_mode: Particle visual size or opacity substitutes for water volume; multiple solvers silently own the same water.

champion.name: JIT M2/M3 conservation law

phenomena.acceptance: Every transfer has explicit source/receiver identity and closed volume residual.

phenomena.meaning: A water surface is the moving boundary between water and air, not a light effect.
phenomena.mechanism: Position, topology, normal, material velocity and thickness must come from the current water state; topology may change only through represented separation.
phenomena.visual_signature: A coherent, continuous wet boundary where water remains connected; authentic silhouette and surface curvature.
phenomena.failure_mode: Individual coarse simulation parcels appear as isolated spheres; disconnected glass shards masquerade as a sheet.

champion.name: Original pool fused Marching Cubes + JIT M3 skin + Particles4All anisotropy

phenomena.acceptance: Compare traced sheet silhouette and connected-component continuity frame-to-frame; preserve best donor.

phenomena.meaning: Heightfields are a compact 2.5D representation of surface motion when one surface height describes a column.
phenomena.mechanism: Conservation/dispersion and obstacle occupancy produce pile-up, side flow, wake and collapse from actual pressure/flow response.
phenomena.visual_signature: Bow pile-up, realistic wave train, evolving stern depression and water following local object motion.
phenomena.failure_mode: Decorative wake textures attached to a moving object, arbitrary ripples or frozen shoreline overlays.

champion.name: heightfieldBEST and THALASSA T3 carpet

phenomena.acceptance: Stationary/tow/sweep tests at matched speeds demonstrate generated wake and fluid displacement without overlay.

phenomena.meaning: A hull excludes liquid volume and forces water to displace around its actual wetted shape.
phenomena.mechanism: Wetted body occupancy and swept trajectory constrain heightfield flow and exchange pressure and impulse.
phenomena.visual_signature: Water climbs the bow, divides around the body and fills its wake as it leaves.
phenomena.failure_mode: One global waterline or an analytic decorative wake standing in for contact.

champion.name: heightfieldBEST computeObstacle; THALASSA occupancy field

phenomena.acceptance: Translation and rotation retain displacement and prevent body tunneling across cells.

phenomena.meaning: Every point of a curved body can meet a different local wave height and normal.
phenomena.mechanism: One authoritative local surface query supplies immersion, gradient, normal, flow and contact for physics and optical wetness.
phenomena.visual_signature: Wet edge conforms to the actual raised/sunken wave around all sides of a sphere.
phenomena.failure_mode: One sampled height at body center creates an unrelated straight wet/dry stripe.

champion.name: JIT R21 shared water-object-contact, historical donor unmounted

phenomena.acceptance: On a tilted asymmetric wave, per-fragment wet contact tracks the physical field and agrees with buoyancy.

phenomena.meaning: Wetness is water adhering to a surface over time, not merely 'below current water level'.
phenomena.mechanism: A film stores deposited liquid mass, drains with body orientation, drips, and evaporates or returns through documented sinks.
phenomena.visual_signature: Emerging sphere remains wet above waterline, with trailing trickles, darkening and direction-dependent gloss.
phenomena.failure_mode: A moving horizontal line instantaneously replaces actual wetness history.

champion.name: JIT Lab R21 metric wetness + heightfieldBEST updateObjectFilm, donor unmounted

phenomena.acceptance: Wave-local deposition, coherent persistent film, drain/drip volume ledger and slow drying without arbitrary disappearance.

phenomena.meaning: 3D fluid is spawned just in time where 2.5D becomes unable to represent folding or detached water.
phenomena.mechanism: Surface steepness, overturn, acceleration and body contact trigger finite events; source water is debited once and given proper velocity/impulse.
phenomena.visual_signature: Crest steepens into a sheet then tendrils and droplets, while the originating surface loses exactly the launched water.
phenomena.failure_mode: Random white splashes attached to a crest with no fluid debit, or unlimited emission at each frame.

champion.name: JIT M2/M3 finite event controller, donor unmounted

phenomena.acceptance: Under a controlled breaking event, source debit matches launch and return; event counts and geometry converge with timestep.

phenomena.meaning: A water sheet is a connected material surface with history until it tears.
phenomena.mechanism: Material coordinate/bond and deformation persist while water advects; tear changes topology rather than retroactively reconnecting arbitrary neighbors.
phenomena.visual_signature: Broad crown stretches to a thin curtain, then narrows into filaments before breakoff.
phenomena.failure_mode: Reconstructed arbitrary triangles, disconnected glass scratches or constant reseeding of connections.

champion.name: JIT M3 temporal ribbons; old pool implicit volume fusion

phenomena.acceptance: Track ancestry and surface topology over time; no rewire after retirement; demonstrate sustained curtain at real impact.

phenomena.meaning: Separated liquid needs a high-detail local 3D solver, not a trillions-of-particles ocean.
phenomena.mechanism: PBF or MLS-MPM integrates particles only in the disturbed local region; pressure and surface tension determine breakup and return.
phenomena.visual_signature: Individual physically sized droplets and coherent ligaments, with gravity, collision and surface tension.
phenomena.failure_mode: Computational parcel rendered as 10-cm opaque foam ball; 3D fluid applied across the entire sea.

champion.name: Particles4All GPU PBF + surface tension (historical donor unmounted)

phenomena.acceptance: Hardware profile, stable particle budget, physical collision, sphere splash and capillary breakup against donor.

phenomena.meaning: Detached liquid becomes part of its receiver water field again on contact.
phenomena.mechanism: Normalised footprint returns volume; momentum may excite radial wave with net impulse zero; dissipation accounted.
phenomena.visual_signature: Splash re-entry creates real local waves, ripples and turbulence with no vanishing pools.
phenomena.failure_mode: Particles disappear when they reach surface without wave feedback, or ledger only marks a boundary.

champion.name: JIT M3 returnParticle and AQUA canonical BFT

phenomena.acceptance: Emit→impact→receiver volume/impulse ledgers close and matched wave amplitude/energy are measured.

phenomena.meaning: Foam is a population of entrained air bubbles in water, not the liquid itself.
phenomena.mechanism: Aeration follows turbulent breaking, air entrainment, buoyant rise, lifetime, accumulation and dissipation.
phenomena.visual_signature: Bright aerated patches appear only where water churns; coherent transparent liquid is still visible elsewhere.
phenomena.failure_mode: All fast liquid is recolored into flat opaque white pellets.

champion.name: Foam Foundry V4.3 historical donor unmounted

phenomena.acceptance: Segment liquid vs entrained gas visual state; measured foam area, lifetime and scattering independent of carrier volume.

phenomena.meaning: Water reflects more light at grazing angles because the air-water interface changes optical impedance.
phenomena.mechanism: Viewing angle, actual geometric normal and physical refractive indices determine angular reflectance; use consistent dielectric polarization/Fresnel approximation.
phenomena.visual_signature: Facing water transmits much of the scene; glancing water becomes mirror-like with correct environmental colors.
phenomena.failure_mode: Fake brightness curve independent of surface normals, sky or index of refraction.

champion.name: POSEIDON optics and older pool ray-shading source

phenomena.acceptance: Test fixed water normal and varying view angle against dielectric reference, with no painted rim.

phenomena.meaning: Refraction is the bending of rays as they cross an interface between air and water.
phenomena.mechanism: Snell's law applied to true interface normal and view ray, traced to the receiving scene/body/terrain; thickness/depth controls path.
phenomena.visual_signature: Background shifts consistently through a curved crown, with angle and thickness; underwater distortions track real surface.
phenomena.failure_mode: Arbitrary UV warp or nearly invisible alpha transparency mistaken for transmission.

champion.name: POSEIDON optics plus original pool ray-geometry shader

phenomena.acceptance: Refracted target displacement changes with shape and camera basis consistently; test against analytic sphere/sheet.

phenomena.meaning: Reflection is radiance from whatever a water-facing reflected ray encounters.
phenomena.mechanism: Physically based reflection from sky, terrain, bodies AND nearby spray/water, including compositing/visibility passes.
phenomena.visual_signature: Splash reflects neighboring sea and sky, and the ocean reflects the splash silhouette where visibility warrants.
phenomena.failure_mode: Splash rendered after water with no path back into ocean reflection, or environment color painted onto splash.

champion.name: POSEIDON scene-aware optics / original pool ray tracing

phenomena.acceptance: Explicit reciprocal visibility test with high-contrast object suspended over water, no incorrect self-reflection.

phenomena.meaning: Water color and visibility depend on the length light travels through liquid and its scattering/absorption.
phenomena.mechanism: Beer-Lambert absorption + participating media; geometric surface depth/thickness, not display-particle diameter, controls transmittance.
phenomena.visual_signature: Thin splash sheets remain transparent but defined by reflections; deep water absorbs strongly by wavelength.
phenomena.failure_mode: Overly transparent no-distortion glass or opaque foam replacing clear liquid.

champion.name: POOL fused surface + POSEIDON optical attenuation

phenomena.acceptance: Transmittance vs known film thickness and camera angle agrees with calibrated absorption model.

phenomena.meaning: A caustic is a focusing or defocusing of transmitted light rays by curved moving water.
phenomena.mechanism: Surface slope/curvature, sun incidence, receiver depth and the refracted-ray mapping/Jacobian drive irradiance concentration.
phenomena.visual_signature: Bright networks move and deform causally with actual waves and depth on bottom/objects.
phenomena.failure_mode: A scrolling random pattern painted onto floor with no dependence on true wave surface or light.

champion.name: POSEIDON/T4R ray/curvature based receiver caustics

phenomena.acceptance: Freeze wave, rotate sun and vary depth; spatial caustic pattern must follow predicted ray mapping and vanish without relevant curvature.

phenomena.meaning: Land topography defines bottom boundaries, channel connections, run-up, overtopping and retreat.
phenomena.mechanism: Depth-averaged conservative flow, wet/dry front treatment, bed elevation, friction and boundary fluxes update volume in each terrain cell.
phenomena.visual_signature: Run-up wets beach, fluid crosses ditch or levee if overtopped, fills basin, retreats appropriately.
phenomena.failure_mode: Clipped water plane, disconnected decorative puddles or water climbing through solids.

champion.name: THALASSA T2 SWE + HybridSplash v43 nearshore donor

phenomena.acceptance: Barrier overtopping/closed basin/wet-dry tests with volume residual, terrain variations and stable CFL stepping.

phenomena.meaning: The ocean can cover planetary scales only if local degrees of freedom appear where needed.
phenomena.mechanism: T0 far-field spectrum, T3 interaction, T2 shore and T4 detached fluid own complementary phenomena, coupled by conservative boundary transactions.
phenomena.visual_signature: Ocean has continuous motion from far field to contact/splash with no obvious seams or energy jumps.
phenomena.failure_mode: Each layer draws independent fake waves with unmatched phase or loses volume at LOD transitions.

champion.name: THALASSA hierarchy + JIT/R22 page conservation

phenomena.acceptance: World-matched handoff at tiers, action-reaction, shoreline seam continuity and real hardware profiling.

phenomena.meaning: Water at the next frame is the evolved state of the same physical field, not a rerolled appearance.
phenomena.mechanism: Numerical advection and persistent histories for surface, sheet topology, foam, body film and return events.
phenomena.visual_signature: Strands thin continuously; wave crests move, wet film ages, caustics follow waves and foam persists appropriately.
phenomena.failure_mode: Popping triangles or randomly resetting splash/caustics despite unchanged forcing.

champion.name: JIT temporal ribbons, HeightfieldBEST, THALASSA temporal states

phenomena.acceptance: Run frame-by-frame time sequence with stable camera, topology events, conservation and flicker metrics.

phenomena.meaning: Water must be a reusable world system receiving actual terrain and moving-body geometry.
phenomena.mechanism: Clean terrain input, query, resource budget, waterbody ownership, physics APIs and finite near-field regions.
phenomena.visual_signature: Any compliant game terrain creates plausible shore/basin interactions and bodies generate correct local effects.
phenomena.failure_mode: Demo-specific island and sphere hard-coded into physics with no general interface.

champion.name: THALASSA modular engine target, not a validated product

phenomena.acceptance: Swap independent terrain maps and compare identical mechanics; benchmark FPS/memory and deterministic queries.

causal_relations.reason: Heightfields evolve the same liquid mass where the free surface remains single-valued
Detached fluid representation carries real water mass outside the heightfield
Reentry must transfer water ownership and impulses back
Displacement and blocked flow create a causal wake
Wetted body geometry defines local contact
Contact deposits a film that persists after exit
Violent contact can exceed heightfield representability
Breaking crests launch only water that cannot remain in the heightfield
Newly launched sheet preserves the original crest and event topology
Tracked sheets determine real air-water interface geometry
As topology breaks, ligaments and droplets become 3D liquid
Detached parcels eventually reenter the heightfield or shoreline
Turbulent collapse entrains air but foam does not replace water volume
A surface normal and optical index give angular reflectance
Surface geometry determines refracted view and light rays
Actual film thickness affects absorption/transmission
Interface normals and scene visibility select reflected radiance
Wave shape and sun angle focus transmitted light onto receivers
Reflected and transmitted energy must be optically consistent
Refracted solar ray mapping creates intensity focus on receivers
Local shoreline height and normal influence body immersion
Actual terrain elevation and wet/dry state must be supplied to engine
Simulation tiers require causal ownership and momentum transfer
Near-field height must remain coherent with far-field ocean waves
Material connections must evolve rather than be remade each frame
Foam accumulation and decay depends on past entrainment
Adhered film retains memory of prior contact
Ray path through film determines what underlying scene remains visible
Same interface must support both transmitted and reflected radiance
Computational resources are allocated by local need rather than ocean extent

promotion_policy.candidate_must: Prove it matches or exceeds incumbent in the incumbent's defining mechanism AND matched real render/physical tests.
reject_when: Uses unrelated scrolling image where existing mechanism derives the effect from water surface
Makes connected water visually into giant computational particles
Replaces per-point surface contact with object-center scalar
Reduces previously demonstrated morphology or temporal coherence without bounded documented tradeoff
comparison_conditions: Fixed frame times and multiple consecutive images
Report physics/visual metrics and GPU time
Keep source champions untouched and reproducible
promotion_policy.risk_policy: Unverified evidence, donor source unavailable, or missing renderer proof => do not declare a new champion or silently replace current winner.
